_meta.indication: VIBATIV is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with complicated skin and skin structure infections (cSSSI) caused by susceptible Gram-positive bacteria
_meta.receipt_date: December 19, 2006 (original NDA received); resubmission (complete response) dated March 13, 2009

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter, multinational trial comparing telavancin 10 mg/kg IV once daily to vancomycin 1 g q12h for 7 to 14 days
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with complicated skin and skin structure infections (cSSSI), primarily due to MRSA
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical Response at Test-of-Cure (co-primary in the All-Treated and Clinically Evaluable populations; 10% noninferiority margin)
pivotal_trials.result: All-Treated cure 72.5% telavancin vs 71.6% vancomycin, difference 0.9% (95% CI -5.3, 7.2); Clinically Evaluable 84.3% vs 82.8%, difference 1.5% (95% CI -4.3, 7.3) — noninferior at the 10% margin

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter, multinational trial (identical design to Study 0017); telavancin 10 mg/kg IV once daily vs vancomycin 1 g q12h for 7 to 14 days
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with complicated skin and skin structure infections (cSSSI), primarily due to MRSA
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical Response at Test-of-Cure (co-primary in the All-Treated and Clinically Evaluable populations; 10% noninferiority margin)
pivotal_trials.result: All-Treated cure 74.7% telavancin vs 74.0% vancomycin, difference 0.7% (95% CI -5.1, 6.5); Clinically Evaluable 83.9% vs 87.7%, difference -3.8% (95% CI -9.2, 1.5) — noninferior at the 10% margin

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥2%) include taste disturbance (33% vs 7% vancomycin), nausea (27% vs 15%), vomiting (14% vs 7%), and foamy urine (13% vs 3%); serious/important risks include nephrotoxicity, infusion-related reactions, and C. difficile-associated diarrhea
target_moa: Semisynthetic lipoglycopeptide antibiotic; inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by interfering with polymerization and cross-linking of peptidoglycan, and binds to and disrupts the bacterial membrane barrier function, giving concentration-dependent bactericidal activity against Gram-positive organisms

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: FETAL RISK — women of childbearing potential should have a serum pregnancy test prior to administration; avoid use during pregnancy unless the potential benefit outweighs the potential risk to the fetus; adverse developmental outcomes observed in 3 animal species at clinically relevant doses raise concerns about potential adverse developmental outcomes in humans

rems.type: REMS approved, consisting of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments

advisory_committee.vote: Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee (AIDAC) voted 21 to 5 that the data demonstrated the safety and effectiveness of telavancin for cSSSI

description.text: Updated clinical trials labeling to include information about patients with baseline Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia in cSSSI and HABP/VABP

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for revisions to the **CLINICAL TRIALS** section (14), Complicated Skin and Skin Structure Infections (14.1) and Hospital-Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia/Ventilator-Associated Bacterial Pneumonia (HABP/VABP) (14.2) subsections to include information about patients with baseline bacteraemia caused by *Staphylococcus aureus*.

summary.text: Telavancin (VIBATIV), a new molecular entity lipoglycopeptide antibacterial, was approved for cSSSI on the third review cycle under a standard review following an approvable letter (October 19, 2007) and a complete response letter (February 20, 2009); approval included a boxed warning for fetal risk, an approved REMS (Medication Guide and communication plan), and was supported by a 21-to-5 AIDAC vote on safety and effectiveness

citations.quote: The original NDA was submitted December 19, 2006, and received a 10-month standard review. The Agency issued an approvable letter on October 19, 2007.
The applicant was issued another complete response on February 20, 2009.
The committee voted 21 to 5 that the data presented demonstrated the safety and effectiveness of telavancin for treatment of cSSSI.

basis.text: Deficiencies related to nephrotoxicity and the risk of teratogenicity; FDA requested more comprehensive HAP renal safety follow-up, follow-up of cSSSI patients with serum creatinine >2x baseline, and submission of a proposed REMS

citations.quote: The majority of the deficiencies in the February 2009 CR letter were related to the findings of nephrotoxicity and the risk of teratogenicity in fetuses of pregnant women exposed to telavancin therapy.
